text:
Jack Roslovic has become one of the few things going right in Toronto. The Columbus native, on his sixth NHL team, has 21 points in 22 games, already more than half of last season's 36 in Edmonton, and since Kirill Marchenko went to injured reserve he has moved onto the first power-play unit and up to about 19 minutes a night. He is one of the fastest skaters in the league by NHL Edge (99th percentile top speed), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says his offense lives in transition: 54% of his shots came off the rush last season.

The caution is in the finishing. He has nine goals on 6.2 expected (the quality of his chances), and his scoring rate is well above the range we'd expect to hold. Still, the Leafs are better with him on the ice, taking 52% of the expected goals at five on five, nearly eight points better than without him. On a team that is winless in seven, that matters. Watch whether the bigger minutes keep the chances coming once the shooting cools.
